r2_s1.text: A friend’s wedding reception. Across the room he is laughing with someone you don’t know, standing a little too close. Your phone lights up in your hand: a message from an old colleague.

choices.label: Walk over and join them

choices.recap: stayed put and read the message
choices.label: Stay put and read the message
Step outside for some air

choices.recap: noticed how many drinks he has had
choices.label: Notice how many drinks he has had

r2_s2a.text: Up close it is harmless. She is a cousin visiting from overseas, and he introduces you with his hand on your back. “He talks about you constantly,” she says. You feel a little foolish.

choices.label: Laugh it off together
Keep wondering anyway

r2_s2b.text: The message reads: “Still thinking about you. Dinner Thursday?” You look up. He is watching you read it.

choices.label: Reply “Maybe”
Delete it and say nothing
Walk over and show him

r2_s2c.text: In the corridor you realise you are checking whether he follows you. He doesn’t. Through the glass doors you can see him still talking, still laughing.

choices.recap: went back and asked him directly
choices.label: Go back and ask him directly
Stay out here and say nothing
Call the colleague back

r2_s3a.text: The band starts a slow song. He holds out his hand, a little awkwardly, the way he did at your own wedding. For a minute it is only the two of you.

choices.label: Dance with him
Hand him your phone before you even open the message

r2_s3b.text: The drive home is quiet. The radio fills the gaps with a song neither of you chose. He taps the wheel, then stops.

choices.label: Ask about the woman at the reception
Look out the window

choices.recap: realised they had nothing to say
choices.label: Realise you have nothing you want to say to him
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

r2_s3c.text: Whatever you said, or didn’t say, it is out in the world now. Your phone is warm in your hand. Across the room he catches your eye and smiles, and you lock the screen.

choices.label: Put the phone away and go to him
Delete the thread
Tell him now, before it grows

r2_s3d.text: He reads the message twice. “Who is this?” His voice is careful, not angry, which somehow makes it harder.

choices.label: Tell him the truth: an old colleague, nothing more

choices.recap: said they didn’t know why it was sent
choices.label: Say you don’t know why they wrote it

textIf.add: You read it over his shoulder at the same time he does.

r2_s4a.text: The song ends. He keeps hold of your hand. “I got jealous tonight,” he says, quietly, as if it embarrasses him.

choices.label: Admit you wondered about him too
Brush it off and change the subject

r2_s4b.text: He turns the radio off. “You’ve been quiet all evening.”

choices.recap: told him what they were really feeling
choices.label: Tell him what you are really feeling
Say “I’m just tired.”
“It’s not just tonight. It’s been months.”
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

r2_s4c.text: In bed, your phone buzzes under the pillow. He lies very still, pretending to sleep.

choices.label: Read it in the bathroom

choices.recap: turned the phone off and faced him
choices.label: Turn the phone off and face him

r2_end_trust.text: You ask, he answers, and the knot loosens. Asking out loud was the hard part.

r2_end_doubt.text: Nothing happened. But the question stays with you all night, and it has no one to answer it.

r2_end_secret.text: You read it under the bathroom light. It is only a few words. It is also the first thing you have kept from him.

r2_end_silence.text: On the ride home, and the night after, you look out of different windows. Neither of you says what you are thinking.

r2_end_confession.text: It is awkward and it costs something. But the thing you were both circling is finally on the table.

r2_d1.text: Nothing happened tonight. That is what you cannot stop thinking about. Neither of you is angry. You are simply somewhere else. At home he asks if you want tea, and you say no before he has finished the sentence.

choices.recap: sat with him while the tea brewed
choices.label: Say yes, and sit with him while it brews
Say you are tired and go up first
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

choices.recap: asked when they last really talked
choices.label: Ask: “When did we last talk about anything?”

r2_d2a.text: You drink it in the kitchen. You talk about the wedding: the band, the speeches, the cake. It is the longest conversation in weeks, and neither of you mentions why it was so hard to start.

choices.label: Suggest a weekend away, just the two of you

choices.recap: enjoyed it, and left it there
choices.label: Enjoy it, and leave it there
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

r2_d2b.text: Weeks pass in small subtractions. Dinner at different times. His shoes by the door and your coat in the hall, like two people who happen to share a key.

choices.label: Move to the spare room “until your cough passes”
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

choices.recap: booked a counselling session and left the card on his plate
choices.label: Book a counselling session and leave the card on his plate
Say nothing. It is easier.
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

r2_d2c.text: He doesn’t argue. He opens his mouth, and the honest answer sits there between you. “Since the recital?” he says at last. “No. Before that.” Neither of you can remember.

choices.label: Reach for his hand

choices.recap: said maybe that was the answer
choices.label: “Maybe that is the answer.”
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

r2_d3a.text: A year goes by. The house is calm, and the calm has a texture, like dust. You eat in front of screens. He has stopped asking about your day and you have stopped telling him.

choices.label: Plan a trip together, to see if you still can

choices.recap: took the job in another city
choices.label: Take the job in the other city. “Just for a while.”
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

choices.label: Carry on as you are
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

r2_d3b.text: The spare room gets a lamp, then a bookshelf, then your things, one drawer at a time. Nobody decides this. He knocks once before he comes in now.

choices.recap: asked to be honest about it
choices.label: Say: “Maybe we should be honest about what this is.”
Rent a small flat “for work”
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

r2_d3c.text: The counsellor asks each of you to name one thing you miss. He says, “The way you laughed at my jokes.” You cannot think of an answer fast enough, and he sees it.

choices.recap: said they missed who they were with him
choices.label: Tell the truth: “I miss who I was with you.”
Say “Everything,” though it is not quite true
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

r2_d4a.text: You both say it at last, in the kitchen, in daylight: this is not working, and nobody did anything wrong. Silence. Then relief, which is the worst part.

choices.recap: agreed to six months apart, no promises
choices.label: Agree to six months apart, no promises
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

choices.recap: agreed to part gently and kept things steady for the children
choices.label: Agree to part gently and keep things steady for the children
Ask for one more year

r2_d4b.text: The flat is quiet in a different way. He visits on Sundays and stays for coffee, careful and polite, like a guest in a house he used to own. Months become a year.

choices.recap: told him they were not coming back
choices.label: Tell him you are not coming back
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

choices.label: Keep calling it temporary
choices.reason: Lived Apart / Separated For Three Years Or More

r2_end_reconnect.text: It is not a fix. It is a decision to turn towards each other on purpose, which is all most marriages that last ever really do.

r2_end_year.text: You both agree, and both quietly start counting.

r2_end_roommates.text: Nothing breaks. That is exactly how it ends: two people, politely sharing a roof.

r2_end_limbo.text: “Temporary” has lasted fourteen months. Neither of you says the other word.

r2_end_years.text: Years pass in separate postcodes. One day a form asks how long you have lived apart, and the number surprises you both.

r2_end_agree.text: You split the furniture and the weekends and sign the same page. It is sad, and it is not cruel. Most people expect it to feel worse than it does.

r2_a1.text: You stop counting at four. He isn’t loud or sloppy. He is charming, which is how you know it isn’t the first time. His glass is refilled before it is empty, and nobody but you seems to notice.

choices.label: Quietly swap his glass for water
Say nothing. It’s a wedding.
Ask him, lightly, if he wants to head home

r2_a2a.text: He notices, and for a second his face goes blank. Then he laughs, a little too loudly. “Are you counting for me now?” In the car afterwards he is very quiet.

choices.recap: said they were worried, not counting
choices.label: “I’m not counting to catch you. I’m worried.”
“Four, since you ask.”

r2_a2b.text: The evening blurs pleasantly for everyone but you. At the end you drive, as you have for a while now, and you realise you can’t remember when that started.

choices.label: Tell yourself it’s only weddings

choices.recap: thought back to when it started
choices.label: Think back: when did you last let him drive home?

r2_a2c.text: “Already?” he says, smiling, but he checks his glass first. He comes, which surprises you. In the car he says, “I know what you were doing back there.”

choices.label: “Then you know why.”
“I was just tired.”

r2_a3a.text: At home you sit at the kitchen table. You say the word you have both been avoiding: that you think the drinking has become a problem. He doesn’t deny it. He looks at his hands.

choices.recap: offered to go with him to get help
choices.label: “I’ll come with you to see someone.”

choices.recap: told him to sort it out himself
choices.label: “You need to sort this out yourself.”

r2_a3b.text: The excuses become routine. A bottle behind the cereal. A “quick one” after work. A promise made on Sunday and forgotten by Wednesday. You start to plan your days around his moods.

choices.recap: covered for him with the children and his mother
choices.label: Cover for him with the children and his mother

choices.recap: told him what it was costing them
choices.label: Tell him calmly what it is costing you

choices.recap: poured out what is in the cupboard
choices.label: Pour out what is in the cupboard

r2_a4a.text: The clinic is plain, with a box of tissues on every table. He sits very straight. The counsellor says it will take months, and that it may not be a straight line. He looks at you before he answers.

choices.recap: took his hand under the table
choices.label: Take his hand under the table

choices.recap: said they would stay, but not at any cost
choices.label: Tell him you will stay, but not at any cost

r2_a4b.text: He promises, and he means it. Three weeks later you find a bottle again. This time he doesn’t hide it. He just looks tired. “I don’t know how to stop,” he says. It is the first honest thing he has said in a year.

choices.recap: said they would find help together
choices.label: “Then let’s find someone who does.”

choices.recap: said they couldn’t keep doing this
choices.label: “I can’t keep doing this.”

r2_end_recovery.text: It is not a cure, only a start. But he said the words himself, and you were in the room when he did.

r2_end_line.text: You tell him you will stay while he tries, and that you will not stay if he doesn’t. It is fair, and it is hard, and you both know which it is more.

r2_end_cover.text: Everyone thinks you are fine. You are very good at this now. The explanations come before anyone asks, and the cupboard stays full.
